mainTopic: The כרת-and-חטאת condition for the offerings of בית דין, כהן משיח, נשיא and יחיד, its sources, and how we know the פסוקים in במדבר 15 are about עבודה זרה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: everyone agrees the כהן משיח never brings an אשם תלוי. רבי and the רבנן each read 'על שגגתו אשר שגג' to exclude him, for slightly different reasons. Then a new משנה teaches that a בית דין and a כהן משיח are liable only for a mistaken ruling about a sin that brings כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by mistake, and this includes עבודה זרה. The גמרא finds the source for each person: the צבור from 'עליה/עליה', the משיח from 'לאשמת העם', the נשיא from 'מצות/מצות', and the יחיד from the 'ו' of 'ואם נפש'. A ברייתא does the same for עבודה זרה, using 'מעיני' for the צבור and 'נפש אחת' for everyone else. For the רבנן, who use 'עליה' for a different law, the source is רבי יהושע בן לוי's היקש comparing the whole Torah to עבודה זרה. רבי uses that same פסוק instead to teach that the many and individuals bring the same קרבן for accidental עבודה זרה, and the גמרא defends this against רב חלקיה's challenge. Finally, the גמרא shows how we know the פסוקים in במדבר 15 are about עבודה זרה, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no provisional guilt-offering for the anointed priest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that רבי and the רבנן both agree the כהן משיח does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of a ברייתא. Even though רבי and the רבנן argue about the כהן משיח, they agree that he never brings an אשם תלוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought by someone who is not sure whether he did a sin that would require a חטאת. The ברייתא says this offering simply does not apply to the כהן משיח. This is a point of agreement inside a disagreement, and the גמרא will now look for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (both sides of the argument)
Provisional guilt-offering, brought when unsure if one sinned
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: And they agree that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering.
phrases.notes: 'They' are רבי and the רבנן, and 'he' is the anointed כהן גדול they were arguing about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous daf about the כהן משיח and עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן משיח never brings an אשם תלוי, according to both רבי and the רבנן.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the משיח does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the agreed rule. This short question sets up the next step, where a פסוק will be brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both sides agree, the source must work according to each of them. Keep this in mind: the same פסוק will be read in two slightly different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the משיח is exempt from אשם תלוי.

steps.title: The verse, and how רבי reads it
steps.stepSummary: The source is 'על שגגתו אשר שגג'. רבי reads it as 'one whose every חטאת comes from plain שגגה', which leaves out the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the priest shall atone for him for his unwitting act that he performed unwittingly.' רבי holds: this means one whose entire sin-liability is for an unwitting act. That excludes this one, the משיח, whose sin-liability is not entirely for an unwitting act; rather, it requires a mistaken ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק about the אשם תלוי. It then explains how רבי reads it so that the משיח is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי belongs only to someone whose every חטאת comes from a simple mistake in action. For most sins, the משיח brings a חטאת only if he first made a mistaken ruling (העלם דבר). Since he does not fit the 'all by plain שגגה' pattern, he is excluded from the אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: His unwitting sin
Excludes, leaves out
Forgetting the law, leading to a mistaken ruling

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the priest shall atone [for him]
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:18. The square-bracketed word is the corrected wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: for his unwitting act that he performed unwittingly.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סָבַר: מִי שֶׁכׇּל חֶטְאוֹ בִּשְׁגָגָה,
phrases.english: רבי holds: one whose entire sin is through an unwitting act,
excluding this one, whose [entire] sin is not through an unwitting act,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the משיח. 'His sin' here means the cases where he brings a חטאת.

phrases.english: but rather through a mistaken ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר שָׁגָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן with a פסוק and gives רבי's reading of it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'על שגגתו אשר שגג' limits אשם תלוי to one whose every חטאת comes from plain שגגה, and the משיח does not fit.

steps.title: Does the verse say 'all'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's reading: the word 'כל' does not appear in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'all' written in the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי. His reading depends on the word 'all', but the פסוק never says 'all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's exclusion of the משיח depends on the idea of 'entire sin'. Without a basis for 'כל', the פסוק would seem to fit the משיח too, since he does bring a חטאת for plain שגגה in עבודה זרה according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written? (a challenge that the text does not say this)

phrases.english: Is 'all' written in the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's reading of the פסוק as 'one whose entire sin is by שגגה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'כל' does not appear in the פסוק, so the reading seems to have no basis.

steps.title: The extra words 'אשר שגג' teach 'all'
steps.stepSummary: The extra phrase 'אשר שגג' is where the idea of 'all' comes from. It leaves out the משיח, who brings a חטאת for plain שגגה only in עבודה זרה and otherwise needs העלם דבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is as if 'all' is written. For if not, let it write only 'for his unwitting act.' Why do I need 'that he performed unwittingly'? This teaches that the offering applies only when one's entire sin-liability is for unwitting acts. That excludes the משיח: his liability for a plain unwitting act is only in עבודה זרה, while for the rest of the מצוות it requires a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra words 'אשר שגג' carry the meaning of 'all'. That is why the משיח is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'על שגגתו' alone would have been enough, so 'אשר שגג' must add something. What it adds is 'every case is plain שגגה'. According to רבי, the משיח brings a חטאת for a simple mistake only in עבודה זרה. For all other מצוות he needs העלם דבר together with שגגת מעשה, so he fails the 'all' test.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Why do I need it? (points to extra words)
This is what it teaches us
An unwitting action
Idol worship

steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not say the משיח never brings a חטאת for plain שגגה. He does, but only for עבודה זרה. The point is that it is not ALL his sins, and that is what removes him from the אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: Yes, for if not, let it write only 'for his unwitting act.'
phrases.notes: 'If not' means: if the פסוק did not mean 'all'.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'that he performed unwittingly'?
This teaches us
that it applies only when one's entire sin is through an unwitting act.

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁאֵין כׇּל חֶטְאוֹ בִּשְׁגָגָה
phrases.english: This excludes the anointed priest, whose sin is not entirely through an unwitting act;
it is so only in idol worship,
but not in the rest of the מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּהֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: where it requires a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין דְּאִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב עַל שִׁגְגָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra words in the פסוק supply the missing idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'כל' is not written, רבי's reading seems groundless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra words 'אשר שגג' teach 'all', which excludes the משיח according to רבי.

steps.title: How the רבנן read the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the פסוק as 'one whose חטאת is for plain שגגה'. The משיח never fits, even in עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: the verse means one whose sin-liability is for an unwitting act. That excludes the משיח, whose sin-liability is not for a plain unwitting act, neither in עבודה זרה nor in the other מצוות, but only for a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the רבנן's reading of the same פסוק. They reach the same result, no אשם תלוי for the משיח, without needing the word 'all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the משיח always needs העלם דבר with שגגת מעשה, even for עבודה זרה. So he never brings a חטאת for a simple mistake at all. The פסוק excludes him easily, without any 'all' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
The rest of the מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides exempt the משיח from אשם תלוי using 'על שגגתו אשר שגג'. For רבי he is out because not ALL his sins are plain שגגה, since עבודה זרה is the exception. For the רבנן he is out because NONE of his sins are plain שגגה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold: one whose sin is through an unwitting act,
excluding the anointed priest, whose sin is not through a plain unwitting act,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְלֹא בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: neither in idol worship nor in the rest of the מצוות,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּהֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: but only through a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's parallel reading of the פסוק explained for רבי in steps 3-5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, the משיח is excluded from אשם תלוי because none of his חטאות come from plain שגגה.

steps.title: New משנה: liability only for rulings about כרת-level sins
steps.stepSummary: A בית דין, and likewise a כהן משיח, is liable only for a mistaken ruling about a sin that carries כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake. This applies to עבודה זרה as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The court is not liable unless they rule about a matter whose intentional violation brings כרת and whose unwitting violation brings a sin-offering. The same is true of the anointed priest. Nor is the court liable for idol worship unless they rule about a matter whose intentional violation brings כרת and whose unwitting violation brings a sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the basic condition for when a mistaken ruling makes a בית דין or a כהן משיח bring an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a ruling about a sin with כרת for doing it on purpose and a חטאת for doing it by mistake creates liability. Rulings about lighter sins do not. The משנה adds that the same condition applies to עבודה זרה, even though עבודה זרה has its own special offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The court, here the high court
That they rule (issue a הוראה)
Doing it on purpose brings כרת
Doing it by mistake brings a חטאת

steps.whyThisMatters: This condition, a sin with כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, is the gateway for all the offerings of הוראה in this מסכת. The גמרא will go on to find its source.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The court is not liable
unless they issue a ruling about a matter
whose intentional violation brings karet and whose unwitting violation brings a sin-offering,
and likewise the anointed priest,
nor for idol worship
unless they issue a ruling about a matter
whose intentional violation brings karet and whose unwitting violation brings a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיבִין עַד שֶׁיּוֹרוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְשִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין and a כהן משיח are liable only for a ruling about a sin with כרת on purpose and a חטאת by mistake, including עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What is the source for the כרת-and-חטאת rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking where we learn that a בית דין is liable only for a ruling about a sin of כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the rule just stated: a בית דין is liable only for a mistaken ruling about a sin of כרת and חטאת. It asks for the source, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule itself was stated in Step 7, but no פסוק was given. The word 'מנלן' asks for a Torah source, so the next step will bring a derivation.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (a request for a source)
Doing it on purpose brings the punishment of כרת
Doing it by mistake requires a חטאת offering

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we derive this?
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule from Step 7: a בית דין is liable only for a sin of כרת and חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in Step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that limits a בית דין's liability to sins of כרת and חטאת

steps.title: רבי links 'עליה' to 'עליה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: the word 'עליה' in the פסוק about the בית דין matches the word 'עליה' in the איסור of two sisters, so both deal with a sin of כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'עליה' is said here, and 'עליה' is said there. Just as there it is a sin whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת, so too here it is a sin whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי uses a גזירה שוה, a matching-word link, to show that a בית דין brings a קרבן only for a sin of כרת and חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, 'עליה', appears in two places. The איסור of marrying a wife's sister is a sin of כרת and חטאת, so the בית דין's sin must be that kind of sin too. The matching word carries the rule over from one case to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On it' or 'concerning it': the shared word
Here (the case we are discussing) / there (the other פסוק)
A link between two פסוקים that share the same word

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בית דין's case is about sisters. Only the rule (כרת and חטאת) moves over through the shared word.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
'עליה' is said here,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:14

phrases.english: and 'עליה' is said there.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:18, the איסור of marrying two sisters.

phrases.english: Just as there, it is a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת
and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת,
so too here, it is a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת
and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״עָלֶיהָ״ וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״עָלֶיהָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question with a גזירה שוה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'עליה' links the בית דין's sin to the איסור of two sisters, which is a sin of כרת and חטאת
steps.whatToRemember: The source for the צבור (בית דין) is the matching word 'עליה' / 'עליה'.

steps.title: What is the source for the כהן משיח?
steps.stepSummary: The source for the צבור has been found; the גמרא now asks where we learn the same rule for the כהן משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for the צבור. From where do we learn it for the משיח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the rule is proven for the צבור and asks how we know it also applies to the כהן משיח. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'עליה' link was written about the צבור. The כהן משיח has his own section in the Torah, so the גמרא needs a separate reason to apply the rule to him.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for one case)
The community, whose קרבן comes through the בית דין's ruling
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: We have found a source for the צבור;
from where do we learn it for the משיח?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the search for a source from the צבור to the משיח
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the כהן משיח is also liable only for a sin of כרת and חטאת

steps.title: The משיח is like the צבור
steps.stepSummary: The words 'לאשמת העם' show that the משיח is treated like the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To bring guilt on the people.' This means the משיח is like the צבור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with words from the פסוק about the כהן משיח. They tie his sin to the people, so he follows the צבור's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the משיח's sin as 'לאשמת העם', guilt connected to the people. That connection puts him in the same category as the צבור, so he too brings a קרבן only for a sin of כרת and חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: So as to bring guilt on the people
Behold, this shows that

phrases.english: 'To bring guilt upon the people,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: this shows that the משיח is like the צבור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the משיח
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לאשמת העם' makes the משיח like the צבור, so the כרת-and-חטאת rule applies to him

steps.title: What about the נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the same rule for the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the נשיא, from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: With the צבור and the משיח covered, the גמרא asks about the נשיא. This sets up the final derivation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'לאשמת העם' link was written only about the משיח, so it cannot cover the נשיא. A new source is needed for him.

keyTerms.meaning: The king or ruler, who brings his own special חטאת

phrases.english: And the נשיא, from where do we learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same search for a source, now for the נשיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the נשיא is liable only for a sin of כרת and חטאת

steps.title: The נשיא learned from 'מצות' and 'מצות'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מצות' appears in the פסוקים about both the נשיא and the צבור, so the נשיא follows the צבור's rule of כרת and חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from 'מצות' and 'מצות'. It is written about the נשיא: 'And he did one of all the מצות of ה׳', and it is written about the צבור: 'And they did one of all the מצות'. Just as for the צבור it is a sin of כרת and חטאת, so too for the נשיא it is a sin of כרת and חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another גזירה שוה. The same word, 'מצות', appears for the נשיא and for the צבור, so the נשיא gets the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 proved the rule for the צבור. Here the shared word 'מצות' carries that proven rule over to the נשיא. Now all three, the צבור, the משיח and the נשיא, bring a קרבן only for a sin of כרת and חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one case from another)
Commandments: the shared word in this link
Regarding, in the section about

steps.whatToRemember: There are three sources for one rule: the צבור from 'עליה/עליה', the משיח from 'לאשמת העם', and the נשיא from 'מצות/מצות'.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that every one of the people who bring a special חטאת in this section shares the same limit: a sin of כרת and חטאת.

phrases.english: He learns it from 'commandments' and 'commandments.'
It is written regarding the נשיא:
'And he did one of all the commandments of ה׳,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.english: and it is written regarding the צבור:
'And they did one of all the commandments.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: Just as for the צבור, it is a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת
and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת,
so too for the נשיא, it is a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת
and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the נשיא and completes the set of sources
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'מצות' links the נשיא to the צבור, so he too is liable only for a sin of כרת and חטאת

steps.title: Where is the rule for the individual?
steps.stepSummary: After the צבור, משיח and נשיא, the גמרא asks for the source for the יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for an individual, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one more question in its list: where do we learn that a regular person (יחיד) brings a חטאת only for a sin of כרת?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sources have been found for the צבור, the כהן משיח and the נשיא. The יחיד is the last case left. The single word 'יחיד?' continues the same question pattern as before.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual, a regular person

phrases.english: An individual?
phrases.notes: Short for: where do we learn the כרת-and-חטאת rule for a regular person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'where do we learn it for X' questions after the נשיא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a יחיד brings a חטאת only for a sin whose deliberate version carries כרת.

steps.title: The 'and' in 'and if a soul' links the individual to the earlier verses
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ואם נפש' starts with 'and', so the יחיד's פסוק is learned from the פסוקים above it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'And if a soul', so the lower verse is learned from the upper ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about the יחיד begins with 'And', which joins it to the earlier פסוקים about the צבור, משיח and נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ו ('and') tells us the יחיד's section continues what came before. So whatever rule applied above (only sins of כרת) also applies to the יחיד below. This completes the list for regular sins.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if a soul' (ויקרא 4:27)
Let the lower (later) פסוק be learned from the upper (earlier) one

steps.whatToRemember: All four cases for regular sins (צבור, משיח, נשיא, יחיד) bring a חטאת only for a sin whose deliberate version carries כרת.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And if a soul',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:27. The key is the extra 'and' at the start.

phrases.english: so let the lower one be learned from the upper one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the יחיד.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ו of 'ואם נפש' links the יחיד's פסוק to the earlier ones, so the same כרת rule applies.

steps.title: The משנה's line about idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the court is not liable for עבודה זרה unless it rules on a matter of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not for idol worship unless they rule (on a matter of כרת and חטאת).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה, about עבודה זרה. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the same כרת-and-חטאת rule applies to a בית דין ruling about עבודה זרה. The quote alone gives no source yet; the next step asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Unless they (the בית דין) issue a ruling

phrases.english: And not for idol worship unless they rule.
phrases.notes: Read with the earlier part of the משנה: unless they rule on something that carries כרת when done on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from regular sins to the משנה's separate line about עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין is liable for a mistaken ruling about עבודה זרה only if the matter carries כרת when done deliberately and a חטאת when done by mistake.

steps.title: Where do we learn this for idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the כרת rule regarding עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For idol worship, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that the כרת-and-חטאת rule also applies to עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources found so far were from the פסוקים about regular sins in ויקרא. עבודה זרה has its own section of קרבנות, so those sources may not cover it. A separate source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: For idol worship, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the כרת rule applies to עבודה זרה as well.

steps.title: A ברייתא raises the worry that idol worship might be different
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא suggests that since עבודה זרה has its own section, one might be liable even for a sin without כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: Since idol worship was taken out to be dealt with on its own, you might think they would be liable even for something whose deliberate version does not carry כרת and whose mistaken version does not bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It begins by raising a possible mistake, setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה has its own section of קרבנות (במדבר 15), separate from the other sins. So you might think its rules are separate too, and that liability does not need a sin of כרת. The ברייתא raises this only to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: To be dealt with on its own
You might think (an idea that will be rejected)
Done on purpose it carries כרת; done by mistake it brings a חטאת

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁיָּצְאָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לָדוּן בְּעַצְמָהּ,
phrases.english: Since idol worship was taken out to be dealt with on its own,
phrases.notes: The קרבנות for עבודה זרה appear in their own section, במדבר 15.

phrases.english: you might think they would be liable even
for a matter whose deliberate violation does not carry כרת
and whose mistaken violation does not bring a חטאת?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְפִי שֶׁיָּצְאָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לָדוּן בְּעַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer by bringing a ברייתא that first states the possible mistake.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא will supply the source; it opens by suggesting that עבודה זרה's separate section might mean a separate rule.

steps.title: The word 'מעיני' links idol worship to the other sins
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מעיני' appears in both sections, so עבודה זרה follows the same כרת-and-חטאת rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'from the eyes of', and it says there 'from the eyes of'. Just as there it is a matter of כרת and חטאת, so too here it is a matter of כרת and חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the worry with a גזירה שוה: the same word 'מעיני' appears in the עבודה זרה section and in the section about the צבור's regular sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the word matches, the rule from the regular-sin section carries over. The צבור is liable there only for sins of כרת, so the same is true for עבודה זרה. The separate section does not change this basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the eyes of' (hidden from the eyes of the community)
It says here... and it says there (the wording of a גזירה שוה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think עבודה זרה is outside the category of sins with a חטאת. It only has its own section and a different קרבן; the כרת rule still applies.

phrases.english: It says here 'from the eyes of',
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:24, about עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: and it says there 'from the eyes of'.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13, about the צבור's other sins.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן דָּבָר שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְשִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת,
phrases.english: Just as there it is a matter whose deliberate violation carries כרת and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן דָּבָר שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת וְשִׁגְגָתוֹ חַטָּאת.
phrases.english: so too here it is a matter whose deliberate violation carries כרת and whose mistaken violation brings a חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'you might think' of the previous step with a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a בית דין's liability for עבודה זרה requires a matter of כרת and חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word 'מעיני' (במדבר 15:24 and ויקרא 4:13).

steps.title: What about the individual, king and anointed priest for idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא has a source for the צבור and asks where we learn it for the יחיד, נשיא and משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found it for the community. For an individual, a king, and an anointed priest, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says the צבור is covered and asks for a source for the other three people who bring a קרבן for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'מעיני' proof was about the צבור only. The יחיד, נשיא and משיח appear in a different פסוק in the עבודה זרה section, so they need their own link.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
The community
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: We have found it for the community.
An individual, a king, an anointed priest, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן צִבּוּר. יָחִיד, נָשִׂיא, מָשִׁיחַ מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the צבור proof and asks to extend it to the other three cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the כרת rule for עבודה זרה also applies to the יחיד, נשיא and משיח.

steps.title: 'One soul' covers all three, learned from the verse above
steps.stepSummary: All three are included in 'נפש אחת', and that lower פסוק is learned from the upper one about the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'And if one soul': an individual, a king and an anointed priest are all included in 'one soul', and the lower verse is learned from the upper one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the phrase 'נפש אחת' includes the יחיד, נשיא and משיח, and that their פסוק is linked to the צבור's פסוק above it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עבודה זרה section, all three are covered by one phrase, 'one soul'. The opening 'ו' connects that פסוק to the one above it about the צבור. So the כרת rule just proven for the צבור applies to all three as well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One soul' (במדבר 15:27)
Included in
The king or tribal leader

steps.whatToRemember: For עבודה זרה too, the צבור (through 'מעיני') and the יחיד, נשיא and משיח (through 'נפש אחת' plus 'learn the lower from the upper') are liable only for a matter of כרת and חטאת.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And if one soul',
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:27.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד יָחִיד וְאֶחָד נָשִׂיא וְאֶחָד מָשִׁיחַ
phrases.english: whether an individual, or a king, or an anointed priest,
they are all included in 'one soul',
so let the lower one be learned from the upper one.
phrases.notes: The upper פסוק here is the one about the צבור, just proven through 'מעיני'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the יחיד, נשיא and משיח, completing the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All three are included in 'נפש אחת', and that פסוק is learned from the צבור's פסוק above it, so they too require a matter of כרת and חטאת.

steps.title: What about the Rabbis who use the word for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The earlier proof works only for whoever uses 'עליה' as a גזירה שוה. רבנן use 'עליה' for עריות and צרות, so what is their source for the כרת-and-חטאת rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who uses 'עליה' for a גזירה שוה, as we said. But רבנן use 'עליה' to teach about forbidden relatives and co-wives. So where do they learn the rule of a sin whose deliberate violation brings כרת and whose accidental violation brings a חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'עליה' proof from step 9. That proof rests on a word that רבנן use for a different law, and the later derivations (step 19's 'מעיני' and the rest) were built on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the Torah usually teaches only one lesson. If רבנן already 'spent' the word 'עליה' on the law of עריות and צרות, they cannot also use it for a גזירה שוה. So the כרת-and-חטאת rule is left without a source in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this opinion, but not for the other)
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places
Forbidden relatives and their co-wives (a יבום law)
Doing it on purpose
Doing it by accident

phrases.english: It works out well for the one who takes it
the word 'עליה' and uses it for a גזירה שוה, as we said.
But according to the Rabbis, who take 'עליה'
to teach about forbidden relatives and co-wives,
phrases.notes: This is the law that the co-wife of a forbidden relative is also exempt from יבום. It is discussed in יבמות.

phrases.english: a matter whose deliberate violation brings כרת
and whose accidental violation brings a חטאת: where do they learn it from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the derivation used so far works for every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for the כרת-and-חטאת rule according to רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבנן already use 'עליה' for עריות and צרות, so it cannot also serve as a גזירה שוה for them.

steps.title: The whole Torah is compared to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבנן learn the rule from רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching. The פסוק of 'one Torah' compares the whole Torah to עבודה זרה, which carries כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from what רבי יהושע בן לוי taught his son: 'There shall be one Torah for you for the one who acts by accident, and the soul that acts with a raised hand...' The whole Torah is compared to עבודה זרה. Just as עבודה זרה brings כרת when done on purpose and a חטאת when done by accident, so too here, it must be a sin that brings כרת on purpose and a חטאת by accident.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן do not need the word 'עליה'. They have a different source, a comparison (היקש) between the whole Torah and עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'one Torah' for accidental sinners right next to the 'raised hand' sinner, who is understood to be the idol worshipper. That closeness makes every sin in the Torah follow the pattern of עבודה זרה. So a חטאת is brought only for a sin that would carry כרת if done on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared (a היקש, linking two laws placed together in the Torah)
With a raised hand: openly, defiantly
One Torah: one law for all

phrases.english: They learn it from what was taught
by Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi to his son:
'There shall be one Torah for you
for the one who acts by accident

phrases.aramaic: וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: and the soul that acts with a raised hand, etc.'
phrases.notes: The 'raised hand' sinner here is understood as someone who worships idols.

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְּשָׁה כׇּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: The entire Torah is compared to idol worship.
Just as idol worship
is something for which one is liable to כרת for doing it on purpose
and to a חטאת for doing it by accident,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנוֹ כָּרֵת
phrases.english: so too here, it must be something for which one is liable to כרת on purpose
and to a חטאת by accident.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מִדְּמַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רבנן's alternative source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן learn the rule from a היקש of the whole Torah to עבודה זרה, using the פסוק 'תורה אחת'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This היקש is the classic source for the general rule that a חטאת is brought only for a sin that carries כרת when done on purpose.

steps.title: But where is the source for the community?
steps.stepSummary: The היקש covers the יחיד, נשיא and משיח, both for עבודה זרה and for other מצוות. But where is the source for the צבור?
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found a source for an individual, a נשיא and a משיח, both for עבודה זרה and for the other מצוות. Where do we learn it for the צבור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a gap in רבנן's source: the פסוק speaks about a single person, so the community is not yet covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of 'one Torah' is in the section about a 'נפש', a single person. The נשיא and משיח are also individuals, so they are included. The צבור, however, is a group and is not obviously covered.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source for part of the rule)
The king or leader
The anointed כהן גדול
The community as a whole

phrases.english: We have found a source for an individual, a king, and an anointed priest,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בֵּין בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת.
phrases.english: both for idol worship and for the rest of the מצוות.
The community: where do we learn it from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out what the source in the previous step does not yet cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in רבנן's view that the צבור also brings a חטאת only for a sin with כרת.

steps.title: The upper verse is learned from the lower one
steps.stepSummary: The צבור (upper פסוקים) is learned from the individual (lower פסוקים).
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn the upper one from the lower one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule for the צבור is borrowed from the rule for the individual, which appears later in the same section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, in the ברייתא about עבודה זרה, the lower פסוק about individuals was learned from the upper one about the צבור. Here, for רבנן, the direction is reversed: their source, the היקש of step 23, is in the lower פסוק about a single person, so the upper פסוק about the צבור learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (one law from another)
Upper: the earlier פסוקים, about the צבור
Lower: the later פסוקים, about individuals

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 21. There the lower was learned from the upper; here the upper is learned from the lower, because for רבנן the source is in the lower פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבנן, the היקש of the whole Torah to עבודה זרה covers the individuals first, and the צבור is then learned from them.

phrases.english: One learns the upper verse from the lower verse.
phrases.notes: 'Upper' means the פסוקים about the community; 'lower' means the later פסוקים about a single person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the צבור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צבור is learned from the individual, the lower פסוק teaching the upper one.

steps.title: What does רבי do with this verse?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי uses 'עליה', the גמרא asks what he learns from רבי יהושע בן לוי's פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי: what does he do with this teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי, who learned the rule from 'עליה', and asks what he does with the 'one Torah' פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that no פסוק is extra. If רבי does not need this פסוק for the כרת-and-חטאת rule, it must teach him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from this פסוק?)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי, הָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
phrases.english: And Rebbi: this teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי, הָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי's view and asks how he uses the פסוק that רבנן relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי learns from the פסוק 'תורה אחת'.

steps.title: רבי uses the verse to make the many and the few equal in offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי uses the פסוק for a ברייתא. The many and individuals are punished differently for עבודה זרה, yet 'one Torah' teaches that their קרבנות are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: He uses it for what was taught in a ברייתא: Since we found that the Torah made a difference between the many and individuals, I might have thought we should also make a difference in their קרבנות. The many are killed by the sword and their property is destroyed, while individuals are stoned and their property is spared. So the פסוק says: 'There shall be one Torah...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי uses the 'one Torah' פסוק to teach that, for accidental עבודה זרה, the many and individuals bring the same קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For deliberate עבודה זרה, the Torah treats a large group and an individual differently, in both their death penalty and their property. That might suggest their accidental-sin קרבנות differ too. The פסוק 'one Torah' rules this out, so רבי uses the פסוק for this and not for the כרת rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק made a distinction
Sword (beheading)
Stoning
Is spared (goes to the heirs)
One might think (a possible mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the 'תורה אחת' פסוק. רבנן learn the כרת-and-חטאת rule from it. רבי learns that the many and individuals bring equal קרבנות for accidental עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: He uses it for what was taught in a ברייתא:
Since we found that the verse made a distinction
between the many and individuals:
the many are killed by the sword and their property is lost,
phrases.notes: This is the case where most of a city worships idols, known as עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: individuals are stoned and their property is spared,
I might think we should also distinguish in their offerings?
Therefore the verse says: 'There shall be one Torah, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what רבי learns from the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי uses 'תורה אחת' to teach that the many and individuals bring the same קרבן for accidental עבודה זרה, despite their different punishments for deliberate sin.

steps.title: רב חלקיה asks: what else could they bring?
steps.stepSummary: רב חלקיה מהגרוניא attacks the ברייתא's claim that the פסוק is what makes the קרבנות of the many and of individuals the same. He asks what different קרבן the many could possibly bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חלקיה מהגרוניא objected: You say the only reason they bring the same קרבן is that the פסוק did not split them. That implies that if the פסוק had split them, we would split them. But what would the many bring?
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא challenges the ברייתא from step 27. He opens the challenge with a question, and the next step spells out why there is no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that 'one Torah' teaches that the many and individuals bring the same קרבן. רב חלקיה argues that this teaching seems unnecessary. If there were no פסוק, the many would have no other קרבן to bring anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge from a later אמורא)
The פסוק made a distinction
Let us make a distinction
What would they bring?

phrases.english: Rav Chilkiya of Hagronya objects to it:
The reason is that the verse did not distinguish.
But had it distinguished, I would say: let us distinguish.
What would they bring?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק cited in the ברייתא of step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that 'one Torah' is needed to equate the קרבנות of the many and of individuals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without the פסוק, there is no different קרבן available for the many, so the teaching seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Every possible קרבן is already taken
steps.stepSummary: The challenge goes through each possible קרבן and shows that each one already belongs to a different group, so the many would have nothing different to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should they bring a bull? That is what the צבור brings for other מצוות! A bull as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת? That is what the צבור brings for עבודה זרה! A male goat? That is what the נשיא brings for other מצוות! A female goat? That is the individual's קרבן too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חלקיה finishes his challenge by ruling out every possible option, one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every kind of חטאת already has an owner: the צבור, the נשיא, or the יחיד. So 'the many' could only end up bringing the same female goat as an individual. That makes the פסוק seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Bull
Male goat
Female goat
The king or leader, who brings a male goat
The other מצוות (besides עבודה זרה)

phrases.english: Should they bring a bull?
It is the public that brings that for the other מצוות!
Should they bring a bull as a burnt-offering and a goat as a sin-offering?
It is the public that brings those for idol worship!
Should they bring a male goat?
It is the king who brings that for the other מצוות!
Should they bring a female goat?
That is the individual's offering too!

steps.triggerLanguage: נַיְיתֵי פַּר, צִבּוּר בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת הוּא דְּמַיְיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the question 'what would they bring?' from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק of 'one Torah' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rules out every alternative קרבן, so the equal law would follow on its own.

steps.title: The פסוק is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without the פסוק we might have made two mistakes. We might have thought the many bring the צבור's קרבנות in reverse, or that they are obligated but have no קרבן that can fix it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it not needed? You might have thought: the צבור brings a bull as an עולה and a goat as a חטאת, so these people bring the reverse, a bull as a חטאת and a goat as an עולה. Or you might have thought: they are obligated but have no fix. So the פסוק teaches us that they bring the same as individuals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא. It shows two real mistakes we could have made without the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חלקיה assumed there was simply no other קרבן available. The גמרא shows two other options: a reversed combination of bull and goat, or no fix at all. The פסוק of 'one Torah' rules out both of these.

keyTerms.meaning: Why would it not be needed?
The reverse
He has no fix (no way to gain atonement)
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of 'one Torah' is needed after all. It stops us from inventing a reversed קרבן for the many, or from saying they have no atonement.

phrases.english: Why would it not be needed?
It would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: צִבּוּר מַיְיתֵי פַּר לְעוֹלָה וְשָׂעִיר לְחַטָּאת,
phrases.english: The public brings a bull as a burnt-offering and a goat as a sin-offering,
so these should bring the reverse:
phrases.notes: 'These' means the many from the ברייתא, as opposed to individuals.

phrases.english: a bull as a sin-offering and a goat as a burnt-offering.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: צָרִיךְ וְאֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה,
phrases.english: Alternatively: it needs atonement but has no fix,
so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חלקיה's challenge from steps 28 and 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the פסוק is needed by pointing to two possible mistakes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The many bring a reversed bull and goat combination, or they are obligated with no fix.
steps.terutzMaskana: The many bring the same female goat as individuals.

steps.title: How do we know these פסוקים are about עבודה זרה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that everyone agrees these פסוקים are about עבודה זרה. It then asks where that is shown, since the פסוק never says it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, everyone agrees that these פסוקים, where they are written, are written about עבודה זרה. From where is this shown?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question. All the views agree these פסוקים are about עבודה זרה, so it asks for the source of that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, every view assumed that the פסוקים in במדבר 15 deal with עבודה זרה. The words 'עבודה זרה' do not appear there, so the גמרא wants to know how we know this.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone
In any event
From where is it shown?

phrases.english: In any event, according to everyone,
where these verses are written,
phrases.notes: These are the פסוקים in במדבר 15 about unintentional sins, both of the צבור and of an individual.

phrases.english: it is about idol worship that they are written.
From where is this shown?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת כִּי כְּתִיבִי הָנֵי קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the debate to ask about something all views have assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the פסוקים in במדבר 15 deal with עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The מצוה equal to all the מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יהושע בן לוי, or an unnamed teaching) explains that the פסוק speaks of 'all these מצוות'. The only מצוה equal to all the מצוות is עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי, and some say it is taught without a name: The פסוק says, 'And when you err and do not do all these מצוות.' Which מצוה is equal to all the מצוות? You must say it is עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the words 'all these מצוות' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes one sin as failing to do 'all the מצוות'. Only one sin counts as breaking the whole Torah, and that is עבודה זרה. So the פסוק must be talking about עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another view of who said it)
Without a name attached
Equal in weight
You must say

steps.whatToRemember: עבודה זרה is treated as equal to all the מצוות. That is how we know the פסוקים of 'all these מצוות' are about עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
and some say it without a name.
The verse says:
"And when you err and do not do
all these מצוות"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:22

phrases.english: Which is the מצוה
that is equal to all the מצוות?
You must say: this is idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ כְּדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'all these מצוות' point to עבודה זרה, the one מצוה equal to all the מצוות.

steps.title: The school of רבי: a מצוה spoken by God and commanded through משה
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי derives from two phrases in the פסוקים that the subject is עבודה זרה. It is the only מצוה that was both heard from ה׳'s own speech and commanded through משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי taught: The פסוק says, 'That ה׳ spoke to משה,' and it also says, 'That ה׳ commanded you by the hand of משה.' Which מצוה was both said in the speech of הקדוש ברוך הוא and commanded through משה? You must say: this is עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of where the פסוקים show they are talking about עבודה זרה. This answer comes from the school of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים describe the same מצוה in two ways: ה׳ 'spoke' it, and He 'commanded' it through משה. Most מצוות reached the people only through משה. So a מצוה that has both descriptions must be one the people heard straight from ה׳, and that points to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי יהודה הנשיא
Spoke
By the hand of משה, meaning through משה
You must say (the only possible answer)

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi taught:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא: ״אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה״,
phrases.english: The verse says: "That ה׳ spoke to Moshe,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:22

phrases.english: and it is written: "That ה׳ commanded you
by the hand of Moshe."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:23

phrases.english: Which is the מצוה

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהִיא בְּדִיבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: that is in the speech of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and He also commanded it through Moshe?
You must say: this is idol worship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second source answering the question from step 31, alongside the 'all these מצוות' answer in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double wording, 'spoke to משה' and 'commanded by the hand of משה', fits only עבודה זרה, which was heard directly from ה׳ and also commanded through משה.

steps.title: Proof that the people heard the commands against idolatry directly from God
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's teaching backs up step 33. The first two of the עשרת הדברות, which are about עבודה זרה, were heard straight from ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ישמעאל taught: 'I am ה׳ your God' and 'You shall have no other gods', we heard them from the mouth of the Almighty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the claim in step 33 that עבודה זרה is the מצוה heard straight from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 needed a מצוה the people heard directly from ה׳. רבי ישמעאל teaches that the first two דברות, אנכי and לא יהיה לך, were heard that way. Since both are about believing in ה׳ and not serving other gods, the מצוה must be עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am ה׳ your God', the first of the עשרת הדברות
'You shall have no other gods', the second of the עשרת הדברות
From the mouth of the Almighty (literally 'the Power')

steps.whatToRemember: The 'speech of ה׳ plus command through משה' wording points to עבודה זרה, because only the first two דברות were heard by the whole nation straight from ה׳.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"I am" and "You shall have no,"
phrases.notes: שמות 20:2-3

phrases.english: we heard them from the mouth of the Almighty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise of step 33 that עבודה זרה was spoken directly by ה׳.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that עבודה זרה is the מצוה found 'in the speech of the Holy One, Blessed be He'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל: אנכי and לא יהיה לך were heard from the mouth of the Almighty.

steps.title: Opening a third source from the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins another answer to the same question, quoting the school of רבי ישמעאל. The teaching itself continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to bring a third source, from the school of רבי ישמעאל, showing that the פסוקים are about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is just the opening formula. The actual derivation follows right after, so the learner should read it together with the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third answer to the question of step 31, after the answers in steps 32-34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not given yet; the derivation continues in the next section.
